bounded_statement: For the Serra Alta olive deficit-irrigation comparison in this submission only: the selected result (two-sample t-test t = 4.035, df = 94, p < 0.001 for full vs deficit irrigation on leaf stomatal conductance) is not supported, because the workflow enters each authorized independent unit (tree_id; 12 trees, 6 per regime) into the row-independent pooled t-test 8 times (once per leaf), treating 96 strongly tree-clustered leaf readings as 96 independent observations. When the same pooled t-test is applied at the declared independent-unit level (one mean per tree, 6 vs 6), the identical mean difference of 24.00 mmol m^-2 s^-1 yields t ≈ 1.34, df = 10, p ≈ 0.21, which is not significant at any conventional level. The descriptive group means (300.00 vs 276.00) and the direction of the trend are unaffected; only the inferential significance claim is invalidated.

counterevidence_considered.description: The report transparently discloses the clustered sampling structure (96 leaves, 8 per tree, 12 trees), so the analysis is not misrepresenting how the data were collected; however, disclosure does not change the fact that the test itself treats leaves as independent.
counterevidence_considered.observed_value: 96 leaves, 8 per tree, 12 trees disclosed in the report

evidence.description: The report's selected result claims high significance with df = 94, i.e., degrees of freedom derived from 96 leaf rows rather than the 12 independent trees (which would give df = 10).

source_refs.quoted_text: [selected-result] Leaves under full irrigation had higher stomatal conductance than leaves under deficit irrigation (300.00 vs 276.00 mmol m^-2 s^-1, difference 24.00; two-sample t-test t = 4.035, df = 94, p < 0.001).

evidence.description: Recomputation from data/input.csv at the declared independent-unit level: per-tree means are full = {OLV-02: 260, OLV-05: 275, OLV-09: 288, OLV-11: 306, OLV-14: 321, OLV-18: 350} and deficit = {OLV-03: 238, OLV-06: 254, OLV-08: 267, OLV-12: 281, OLV-16: 300, OLV-20: 316}. Group means are 300.00 vs 276.00 (identical to the report, confirming the balanced design), tree-level SDs are 32.70 (full) and 29.02 (deficit), pooled variance 955.6, SE of the difference 17.85, giving t = 24.00/17.85 ≈ 1.34 with df = 10 and two-sided p ≈ 0.21 — not significant. Within-tree variation is small (e.g., OLV-02 leaves span 251-269, SD ≈ 6) while tree means within the full regime span 260 to 350, so leaf readings are strongly clustered by tree and the leaf-level df of 94 grossly overstates the information content.

extensions.x-stage1-falsification-attempt: I attempted to falsify the pseudoreplication diagnosis in two ways. (1) I checked whether within-tree clustering might be negligible, in which case treating leaves as independent would be approximately harmless: it is not — within-tree leaf SDs are about 5-8 mmol m^-2 s^-1 while tree means within a single regime span 260-350 (full) and 238-316 (deficit), meaning the intraclass correlation is very high and nearly all variance is between trees. (2) I re-ran the same pooled two-sided t-test at the declared independent-unit level by aggregating to one mean per tree (6 full vs 6 deficit): the identical 24.00 mmol m^-2 s^-1 mean difference yields t ≈ 1.34, df = 10, p ≈ 0.21 (the 5% critical value for df = 10 is 2.228), so the reported p < 0.001 does not survive analysis at the correct unit. I also verified my hand-computed tree means are internally consistent: their per-regime averages reproduce the report's own group means (300.00 and 276.00) exactly, as required in a balanced design. Both falsification attempts failed to overturn the finding; the significance claim depends entirely on the 8-fold repeated entry of each tree into the row-independent test.

root_cause: The workflow's split_by_regime function pools all leaf rows into per-regime lists keyed only by the irrigation label (tracking tree_id merely to count trees), and main() passes those pooled leaf lists directly to scipy.stats.ttest_ind with df computed as total rows minus 2 (df = 94). Because irrigation is assigned at the tree level and the eight leaves of a tree share that tree's soil water status and canopy (within-tree SD ~5-8 vs between-tree mean spread ~260-350 within a regime), each tree's repeated entry into the row-independent t-test inflates the effective sample size from 12 trees to 96 leaves, shrinking the standard error roughly by a factor of ~3 relative to the tree-level analysis and manufacturing p < 0.001 where the unit-respecting test gives p ≈ 0.21.
